prompt: Drive a JList through its DefaultListModel: add and remove items and manage the selection. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Swing's list components follow the model-view split: DefaultListModel owns the data and fires change events, while JList only draws whatever the model currently reports. That is why addElement and removeElement go to the model but setSelectedIndex and getSelectedValue go to the JList -- selection is a property of the view. removeElement conveniently returns a boolean saying whether the value was found, which is exactly the answer removeItem owes its caller. Clearing the selection for an unknown value avoids the classic bug of calling setSelectedIndex(-1) by accident and leaving a stale selection behind.
hints: Every data operation goes through model: addElement, getSize, removeElement, indexOf.
DefaultListModel.removeElement already returns true or false depending on whether the value was there, so removeItem can return its result directly.
model.indexOf returns -1 when the value is absent -- branch on that and call list.clearSelection() rather than list.setSelectedIndex(-1).
